learningObjective: State the role of an operator dispatcher in an ML runtime (selecting an implementation based on device, dtype, layout) versus the role of an executor (issuing work on the device).

canonicalClaims.claim: An operator dispatcher routes a logical op call to a concrete implementation based on a key set (device, dtype, layout, autograd, functorch, etc.); the executor issues the resulting kernel on the device.
conditions: The runtime maintains an operator registry mapping keys to implementations.
Dispatch happens at op-call time in eager mode; in a compiled graph the dispatch is baked in.
nonImplications: Does not imply the dispatcher performs synchronization or allocation.
Does not imply every framework exposes a user-facing dispatcher API.

misconceptions.claim: The dispatcher synchronizes streams before every op.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Stream and event synchronization is a runtime API concern, not a dispatch concern.
Allocation is the allocator's job; the dispatcher only routes to the kernel, which then requests output memory from the allocator.
Fusion is a compile-time transformation; the dispatcher acts on individual op calls at run time.

misconceptions.claim: The dispatcher makes eager mode as fast as compiled mode.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Per-op dispatch has measurable overhead; eliminating it via compilation is one motivation for torch.compile.
